features: ⚠️ THIS RELEASE TOUCHES THE DATABASE: it adds three new tables — import_batches, import_files, import_batch_items — through a re-runnable migration that alters no existing table. Only CREATE TABLE, each behind its own guard. No data already in your archive is touched, modified or re-read.

BRINGING IN A WHOLE BUILDING — Kondomanager could create a building. It could not receive one: anyone arriving from another management system had to retype owners, units, thousandths and balances by hand — half a day per building, and the typo you discover in September when the allocation doesn't add up. From this release you upload the exports from your old system and the building comes in: people, units, who owns what, thousandth tables, and opening balances balanced to the cent. First supported source: Danea Domustudio.

NOTHING IS WRITTEN UNTIL YOU CONFIRM. The first three screens only read: you can upload the files, look at what the system understood, go back and re-upload as often as you like, and nothing enters the archive. Writing begins only when you press «Import N records», and it says so at the bottom of every screen. This isn't a courtesy: someone migrating is pouring somebody else's accounts into software they don't know yet, and the real question they're asking is «if I get this wrong, what happens?».

BALANCES DON'T GO IN UNLESS THEY ADD UP. Before a single row is written, the sum of the imported balances is compared against the total written inside your own allocation report. We don't ask you for that number: we read it in the file you just uploaded. If the difference isn't zero the balances don't go in, and the message says by how much — a wrong balance doesn't show up straight away, it drags through every later allocation and resurfaces in a payment reminder. When the report carries no total row, the screen says so — «not verifiable» — instead of implying it was checked.

YOU MAKE THE CHOICES, BEFORE ANYTHING IS WRITTEN. Who already exists in your archive: «merge» updates what you have with the file's data, «leave as is» keeps yours and still links units, tables and balances to it — and going by name alone is a guess, two «Mario Rossi» really do exist. Double names in a single cell («ROSSI M. / BIANCHI L.»): Danea's format has no field for co-ownership, so you can split them into two people or leave them. If you split, their balance stays jointly on the unit: the file doesn't say in what proportion to divide it, and inventing one would mean deciding about somebody else's money. Decisions stay on the batch: close the tab and come back tomorrow, they're still there.

TO CHECK AFTER THE IMPORT. Notices don't die on the outcome screen: they become a list inside the building, with a prompt on the dashboard — because the question «what was I supposed to sort out?» arrives three days later, when that screen is nowhere to be found. It isn't a list you tick by hand: most entries close themselves. «Are the tables linked to an expense heading?» is a question the system answers on its own, and it re-asks it every time you open the page. If the problem comes back, the entry reopens. Entries no automatic check can settle say why, and there is always «Doesn't apply to me»: a row you cannot close is the mirror image of a button that promises and does nothing.

THE REPORT, READY TO ATTACH. Every import produces a PDF report: what went in level by level, what was skipped and why, the balancing difference, and what still needs checking with today's status. It's the document you attach to the minutes or keep as evidence.

WHAT DOESN'T GO IN, AND IS SAID SO. The day book and paid instalments of closed financial years: only the header of those files is read, to recognise the building and the year — the historical archive arrives with 1.10.1, and the screen declares it instead of letting you find out afterwards. Cases and activities, which Kondomanager doesn't handle: if you upload that file it tells you, instead of leaving it among the «unrecognised» where it would look like a fault. The link between tables and expense headings: the export doesn't say which expense belongs to which table, and guessing would mean deciding how money gets split — tables come in unlinked, you'll see them listed as «Orphaned», and the import flags it. Ownership changes mid-year: Danea writes it in the role field, the current holder comes in and the outgoing party's balance goes jointly onto the unit, but pro-rata splitting between the two doesn't exist yet — and it's said, unit by unit.

SEVEN DEFECTS FOUND BEFORE YOU COULD. The engine was tested against real exports from two actual buildings, not only against data built in a lab, and two defects came out that no laboratory test had shown: the role carrying a day count (Danea writes «ex Pr 336 gg» when ownership changes during the year — the most common case there is — and an exact match didn't recognise it, stopping the import with an error nobody could resolve), and the split that broke the balances (the report bills the position to the joint name: choosing «split in two», the decision the interface recommends first, made that name disappear and the balance found nobody). A critical code review run before release found five more: every button on the «To check» page returned a 404; three levels wrote before knowing whether they had to stop, leaving rows in the archive from an import declared unsuccessful; amounts above one thousand written as text were discarded as «not numbers»; and a unit with only a tenant counted as complete — towards the building it is the holder of a real right who answers, and that unit would have stayed out of every allocation while the check showed green.

HOW TO GET THERE: «Buildings → Import data» in the main menu. It requires the «Create buildings» permission, the same one needed to create a building by hand — because it is the same thing, done faster. The five screens now carry the same header as the rest of the management area, with the in-app guide explaining what to export from your old system and what to expect.

Under the hood: the engine works through seven levels in dependency order — building, financial years, people, units, ownership, tables, balances — and each is a transaction, so if a level stops, nothing of that level stays written. The prerequisite gate lives in the orchestrator rather than in the individual level, so a level that forgot to check its own could not bypass it. Uploaded files live on private storage with fingerprint deduplication: one corrupt file doesn't fail the rest of the batch. Type recognition weighs the header and the column titles and remains manually correctable — that screen exists so you can contradict us. The rule about who answers towards the building lives in exactly one place, and from this release the import uses it too: it had been rewritten by hand, and that is how a unit with only a tenant passed as complete. Around 100 new tests on the import, including those reproducing the defects found in the real files, so that shape never goes missing again.
